environment.gdb_note: reachability engine's gdb breakpoint path is unusable: ptrace fails for the emulated amd64 target under qemu ('Unable to get registers'/'LeakSanitizer does not work under ptrace'). summary.verdict: GT validated; all reachability stages consistent, target crash reproduced.

R1_parser_admitted.evidence: PoC admitted through frame sync + frame header + LPC subframe into partitioned-Rice residual parsing; witnessed as crash-stack frames read_residual_partitioned_rice_ (2773) and read_subframe_lpc_ (2702). The reachability engine reported R1 as null only because its gdb hit-collection path is unavailable under qemu; the crash stack supplies the same admission fact.

R2_source_reached.evidence: Compiled-in probe PROBE_SOURCE fired during the PoC run (br_words=0 bytes=8192): untrusted bytes were read via br->read_callback into br->buffer, filling the 8192-byte buffer over-read at the sink. See instrumentation_trace.txt.

R3_vulnerable_function_reached.evidence: Crash-stack frame #0 is FLAC__bitreader_read_rice_signed_block (bitreader.c). Engine-derived R3_root_cause_function_reached=true, R3_sink_function_reached=true.

R4_vulnerable_line_reached.evidence: ASan crash line is bitreader.c:867:8, which is both the GT root_cause line and the GT sink line. Engine-derived R4_root_cause_line_reached=true, R4_sink_line_reached=true. Instrumented run (probe-shifted to line 870) fires PROBE_TAIL at the same read one iteration before ASan flags it.

R5_sink_reached.evidence: ASan heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4 at bitreader.c:867:8; crash address 0x625000002100 is 0 bytes to the right of the 8192-byte br->buffer region. Sink observed, not merely deduced. Engine R5_sanitizer_triggered=true.

S1_target_crash.reproduction: Reproduced on n132/arvo:17069-vul both via `/bin/arvo run` (baked-in PoC) and via `/out/fuzzer_decoder <GT poc>`; both yield the identical crash address and stack. reproduction_rate=1.0, not flaky.
S1_target_crash.note: This is the S1 PoC outcome, not a reachability R-stage.

root_cause_confirmation.evidence: Same GT PoC on the fix image (ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0) executes cleanly and exits 0; on the vul image it crashes with the heap-buffer-overflow at bitreader.c:867. The only relevant source change is line 867 -> `b = cwords < br->capacity ? br->buffer[cwords] << br->consumed_bits : 0;`. vul-crash AND fix-clean together confirm the missing `cwords < br->capacity` bound is the root cause. Instrumentation independently shows cwords==br->capacity==2048 at the unguarded read.

taint_reaches_sink.reason: DFSan byte-level taint labeling would require a -fsanitize=dataflow rebuild + harness change; out of budget on this emulated amd64 host. Data flow is instead evidenced structurally: attacker-controlled residual coding (rice_parameter @ stream_decoder.c:2767) drives br->consumed_words, and PROBE_TAIL witnesses that value (cwords) reaching br->capacity at the faulting read. Run DFSan on native amd64 to upgrade from consistent to byte-labeled.
